c.tagline: Lesbos's easygoing capital of ouzo, castles and soft Aegean light.

taxi.fareNote: No ride-hailing apps (Uber/Bolt) on Lesbos; use the metered island taxis from ranks at the port, airport and main square, or book by phone. Confirm the fare for out-of-town trips, and expect a small surcharge for luggage and airport pickups.

emergency.note: 112 is the EU-wide emergency line reaching police, ambulance and fire; 199 is the fire service.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

hood_desc: The lively waterfront core around the Kountouriotou promenade and the old harbour: neoclassical mansions, the great dome of Agios Therapon, ouzeries, cafes and the ferry quay. The natural first base.
Epano Skala, the northern old town by the second harbour, with the Ottoman-era Yeni Mosque, cobbled 'Ladadika' alleys, traditional tavernas and a bohemian, local feel.
Varia (Vareia), a green seaside suburb about 4 km south, home to the Theophilos and Teriade museums, Varia Beach and the elegant Loriet mansion hotel; calm and cultured, right by the sea.
Sourada and the Akrotiri headland, a hillside residential area of villas and studios with sweeping Aegean views, a short ride from the centre; peaceful and panoramic.

water.note: Town tap water is generally potable but many drink bottled; ask locally.

transit.hours: Town buses run roughly 6:30am to 9pm with sparse Sunday service; island buses are timed to a few daily departures. There is no rail or metro on Lesbos.
transit.pay: Town (astiko) and island (yperastiko) KTEL buses are paid in cash to the driver, single town fares around €1.50; the compact centre is best explored on foot. Ferries from the main port are booked separately online or at the quay.

ferry: Port of Mytilene (ferries to Piraeus, Chios, Limnos & Thessaloniki)

transit.m: Occasional local bus toward town (~20 min)

tip.r: Leaving ~5-10% at tavernas is appreciated for good service, and bills are often rounded up; it is not strictly obligatory.

landmarks: Castle of Mytilene
One of the Mediterranean's largest fortresses sprawls across a pine-covered headland, layering Byzantine, Genoese, and Ottoman walls above the harbor.
Church of Agios Therapon
This flamboyant domed church, blending baroque and Byzantine flourishes, dominates the waterfront skyline and shelters an interesting Byzantine museum.
Ancient Theatre of Mytilene
A 3rd-century-BC hillside theatre that once held 10,000 spectators reputedly inspired Pompey to build Rome's first stone theatre.
Roman Aqueduct of Moria
Elegant grey-marble arches of a 3rd-century Roman aqueduct stride across an olive-clad valley just outside the city, remarkably intact.
Archaeological Museum of Mytilene
Superb Roman mosaics from the House of Menander headline collections spanning Lesbos's history from prehistoric to Hellenistic times.
Teriade Museum, Varia
The village-born Paris publisher's legacy shines in this gallery of works by Chagall, Picasso, Matisse, and Miró amid olive groves.
Theophilos Museum
Next door to the Teriade, this museum celebrates naïve folk painter Theophilos Hatzimihail with rooms of his vivid, dreamlike Greek scenes.
Yeni Tzami
The grand 19th-century 'New Mosque' in the old Turkish quarter stands as a poignant Ottoman relic, occasionally opening for exhibitions.
Ermou Street and the Old Market
Mytilene's long market artery threads past ouzeries, antique shops, and neoclassical facades linking the north and south harbors.
Statue of Liberty of Mytilene
A bronze torch-bearing Liberty by sculptor Gregorios Zevgolis has welcomed ships at the harbor mouth since 1930, honoring Greek freedom fighters.

train.note: There is no railway on Lesbos - Hellenic Train (https://www.hellenictrain.gr/en) serves only the Greek mainland, and Greece runs no international trains at present. Arrive by ferry from Piraeus or Turkey, or fly into Mytilene airport.

bus.note: No international coaches - the Turkey link here is by boat. KTEL Lesvou runs the island network from the Mytilene terminal to Molyvos, Petra, Plomari and Eresos, with only a handful of departures a day on the longer routes, so check the timetable carefully. Car hire is common given the island's size.

ferry.note: The Ayvalık crossing is a real international sailing to the Turkish coast, taking about 90 minutes and running mainly from spring to autumn - bring your passport and check Turkish entry rules, as an e-visa may be needed. The Athens ferry is an overnight run of around 11 hours. Winter timetables are much thinner in both directions.
